chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ahmad ibn 'Umar al-Hallal said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to pray the two rak'ahs of the obligatory Tawaf and did not remember until he arrived at Mina. He said, 'He returns to the Maqam Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and prays them.'

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The two rak'ahs of prayer performed after the obligatory Tawaf
key_terms.مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: The Station of Abraham, a specific location in the Masjid al-Haram where the two rak'ahs are prayed
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a location near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets the two rak'ahs of Tawaf until reaching Mina?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the compensatory procedure for the two rak'ahs of Salat al-Tawaf when a pilgrim forgets them until reaching Mina, a key stage of the Hajj itinerary. The Imam’s directive to return specifically to the Maqam Ibrahim underscores the sanctity of this location as the designated site for this prayer, distinguishing it from other potential spots in the Haram. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on rectifying missed obligatory acts with precision, ensuring the validity of the Tawaf despite the delay.
